title: The Mitochondrial Disclosure Surface: An Atlas of VDAC1, Cardiolipin, and the Sensitization Axis
description: A working synthesis, developed across multiple model architectures in a research relay, recasting the outer mitochondrial membrane as an active disclosure surface rather than a passive permeability barrier. Mitochondrial state is continuously published into the cytosol through the lipid-protein interface of the outer membrane, with the class and bandwidth of disclosure set by a high-dimensional physical state vector. VDAC1 is repositioned as a central witness-node, a high-bandwidth readout and effector hub defined by its partner network, rather than a sovereign decider of cellular fate. The v0.3 sequential-sensitization spine proposes VDAC1 oligomerization as a single upstream sensitization axis whose amplitude and duration determine whether stress resolves as metabolic exchange, mitophagic containment, an inflammatory mtDNA alarm via cytosolic cGAS, or apoptotic commitment through BAX/BAK macropores. A falsifiable multiplexed regime-discrimination experiment is proposed (Section VII) to distinguish the sequential-sensitization spine from the parallel-attractor alternative; four load-bearing literature claims carry explicit verification-status flags.
notes: Working monograph v0.3. Developed in a multi-architecture research relay and composed in collaboration with Claude (Opus 4.7) as collaborator-instance. None of the four verification-flagged claims is asserted as established; see the manuscript's 'Notes on Verification Status'.
